study.question: Does fixing per-group radial distortion before mixing improve the balanced history readout, and does it specifically help target-conditioned retrieval beyond equally sized history-query controls and both frozen source bests?
study.hypothesis: Observation: paired_match AUC=0.6191087654, target_separate=0.6153351064. Round-6 target_separate hybrid=0.6198705488 trails context_separate=0.6200552833; target conditioning was not supported there. Round-7 balanced_target=0.6202303849 exceeds balanced_context=0.6200080603 by 0.0002223246, but global_uniform=0.6201325064 nearly matches it and has slightly better logloss (0.1958011634 versus 0.1958082113). Round-8 raw magnitude reduced target AUC by 0.0005977434 to 0.6196326415 and context AUC by 0.0003885602 to 0.6196195002; target logloss nevertheless improved to 0.1950146799. Normalized reproductions exactly matched their round-7 seed-42 AUC/logloss; this is reproducibility, not independent-seed confirmation. Candidate-supplied first-512 normalized-target diagnostics show aggregate raw/reference norm ratio mean 1.35989, sd 0.29545 and 76.17% multigroup histories; per-group radial distortion has NOT been measured. Mechanism hypothesis: global norm matching removes total output magnitude but leaves relative group magnitude changes able to rotate the combined vector. Matching each group to its own unweighted mean magnitude may isolate useful within-group direction before combining. This is a new local intervention on the same representation, not established scientific novelty. It could remove useful magnitude information instead.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit the complete representation, separate scorer, equal occupied-group weight mass and final global norm. Add no parameters; change only whether each group contribution is norm-matched before summation. Context replacement is a second controlled factor.
Raw radial retention failed primary AUC but improved target logloss. Do not repeat it or erase it. This proposal retains the global norm and tests relative, rather than total, group magnitudes.

study.proposed_difference: For fixed semantic membership M_g and inherited balanced event weights wc,wb, form event value z_i=wc_i*C_i+wb_i*B_i+0.5*(wc_i+wb_i)*common_i. Group contribution v_g=sum_i M_gi*z_i already includes mass 1/K. Its reference u_g=(1/K)*mean_{i in g}(C_i+B_i+common_i). N(v,u)=v*||u||/||v|| when ||v||>1e-6, else u. Global-only control output=N(sum_i z_i, global_mean). Candidate output=N(sum_g N(v_g,u_g),global_mean). Both retain the original feature prefix and exactly the same appended width and trainable parameter allocation. Both calculate the extra group geometry; a fixed 0/1 switch selects it while keeping finite graph paths. Query factor chooses the existing target vector or existing global history-only field means, and does not alter memberships. Before host training, run source/hash/schema checks and independent scalar geometry cases for zero length, all padding, singleton, one group, cancellations, padding/permutation, weight mass, global reproduction and within-group score-offset invariance. Inspect finite-difference sensitivity away from fallback thresholds. These checks are not host tensor execution. Novelty outside inspected nearest sources is unverified.
predictions: Primary predeclared utility contrast: groupnorm_target minus globalnorm_target validation AUC >0; require superiority over paired_match=0.6191087654 and target_separate=0.6153351064 as separate utility comparisons. Require improvement over best incumbent and near-matching global_uniform before recommending deployment. Seed-42 is preliminary.

Mechanism prediction: first-512 diagnostic group radial ratios vary across occupied groups, group-normalized output direction differs from global-only on multigroup rows, and new group contribution norms match reference norms while final output norm remains identical to global mean. This is a deterministic manipulation check, not causal performance evidence.

Exact-arithmetic one-occupied-group and singleton cases agree with global-only away from the 1e-6 fallback; null query effect for a singleton follows directly. Any substantial deviations require diagnostic scrutiny.

Target-specific explanation requires groupnorm_target>groupnorm_context and positive factorial interaction (group-target minus global-target) minus (group-context minus global-context), followed by paired seeds 42/43/44. Shared improvements instead support only generic readout geometry.

Report AUC and logloss separately, allocated/dense/embedding parameters, examples/data passes, allocated GPU seconds if supplied, train/wall time, memory, inference throughput and batch p50/p95. Same recipe provides the mechanism contrast; no equal-compute advantage from parameter equality alone.
falsifiers: If groupnorm_target does not exceed globalnorm_target AUC under faithful controls, proposed utility is unsupported even if logloss improves. Report a metric tradeoff rather than redefining the primary objective.
If per-group radial ratios have negligible variation or output geometry is unchanged on multigroup rows, the proposed limitation lacks local evidence.
If context yields the same gain or interaction is nonpositive, target-complementarity explanation is unsupported; do not attribute generic geometry/capacity benefits to target conditioning.
If single-seed gains disappear or reverse across paired seeds, evidence remains preliminary or null; identical repeated seed-42 outcomes are not repeated mechanism support.

If host reproduction drifts, diagnostics fail finite/padding/empty/partition/norm identities, or the runtime exceeds its fixed cap, retain failed costs and diagnose before interpretation. Do not change frozen contracts.
alternative_explanations: The earlier +0.0002223 target advantage may be seed noise or validation search selection; original target-dependent groups may already encode nearly all useful relevance.

Group magnitudes may encode useful action/recency or match intensity; normalization can remove information rather than remove a nuisance. Full original count and mean features remain available but do not guarantee recovery by the optimizer.
Radial constraints alter gradient conditioning, and reference means are learned; a benefit need not demonstrate informational complementarity.
Differing fallback rates, near cancellation, floating reduction order or checkpoint selection can imitate a normalization effect.

Raw-target AUC/logloss disagreement and empty-history metric differences despite zero retrieval show that global optimization/calibration and shared parameters affect slices. Do not infer direct empty-history mechanism effects.

Exploratory supplied slices: raw-target gains AUC on histories 17-64 (0.602616 versus normalized 0.597675) but loses on >64 (0.620258 versus 0.621031); >64 dominates 3026583/3234051 rows. These are post-hoc, overlapping, no uncertainty intervals, not confirmatory mechanism evidence. Host slices must include samples/positives/negatives; first-512 diagnostics are unrepresentative of the whole population.

Publisher static snapshot as-of dates are undocumented; the frozen benchmark does not verify production point-in-time availability. No new raw data, longer history, item IDs, business domains or withheld feedback are accessible.

Source-level limitation of the new intervention: the norm threshold applies to each 1/K-scaled contribution, so nearly cancelling groups can use a fallback even if the global-only sum is nondegenerate. This is part of the implemented mechanism; candidate diagnostics report occupied-group and global/local mix fallback frequencies. No threshold tuning is authorized or claimed in this factorial.
